Ashok Kumar And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17
August, 2023
Author: Rajiv Gupta

Bench: Rajiv Gupta
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:166181
Court No. - 86
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 28777 of 2023
Applicant :- Ashok Kumar And 2 Others

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Vinod Kumar Kushwaha
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ambrish Kumar Kashyap
Hon'ble Rajiv Gupta,J.
1.

No objection/short counter affidavit filed on behalf of opposite party No. 2 today in Court, is taken
on record.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA for the State, Ms. Pramila Singh holding brief of Sri Ambrish Kumar Kashyap, learned counsel for the opposite party No. 2 and perused the record.

3. This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings of Case No. 1148 of 2011 (State vs. Ashok Kumar and others) arising out of Case Crime Ashok Kumar And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48419365/
1 No. 395 of 2011, under Sections 323, 498A, 506 IPC and 3/4 of D.P. Act, P.S. Tilhar, District- Shahjahanpur, pending in the court of Civil Judge (Junior Division) Tilhar, Shahjahanpur.
4.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that opposite party No. 2 is the wife of applicant No. 1 and applicant Nos. 2 and 3 are his parents and on account of matrimonial discord, the present criminal case was instituted against the applicants, however subsequently, with the intervention of the respected members of both the families and society, they have amicably and genuinely settled all their disputes and differences and they do not have any grievance against each other.

5. Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that after framing of the charge in the instant case, the trial proceeded and the statement of P.W.-1 and P.W.-2 was recorded on 27.5.2015 and the trial was in progress, however subsequently, on 14.3.2020, father of opposite party No. 2 passed away and the applicants participated in his funeral and thereafter dispute between the parties was settled and since 19.2.2022 opposite party No. 2 is living with her husband at her matrimonial home alongwith her two children and they are leading a happy married life.

6. Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that opposite party No. 2 was recalled for further cross examination and on 27.3.2023 and she was further cross examined, in which she has resiled from earlier statement and has stated that all dispute between the parties has already been settled and she has restored her relations with her husband and are living together as husband and wife for the last one and a half years and she does not want to further prosecute the applicants.

7. Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that in view of the changed circumstance when the opposite party No. 2 alongwith her two minor children has restored their relations and are living peacefully with her husband and other family members, the entire proceedings be quashed.

8. Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 has also appeared and has filed an affidavit on behalf of opposite party No. 2 and in paragraph-16 of the said affidavit, it has been categorically stated that all disputes between the parties have been settled and since 19.2.2022 applicant No. 1 and opposite party No. 2 are living together as husband and wife and now she does not want to further prosecute the applicants.
In paragraph-20, it has been further submitted that she has no objection if the entire proceedings are quashed.
9. Learned AGA could not dispute the aforesaid facts.

10. This Court is not unmindful of the judgements of the Apex Court in the cases of :-
1. B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another (2003) 4 SCC 675.
2. Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation [2008) 9 SCC 677].

Reference may also be made to the decision given by this Court in Shaifullah and others Vs. State of U.P. and another [2013 (83)

sentences.text: 11. In the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that all dispute between the parties have already been settled and applicant No. 1 and opposite party No. 2 have restored their relations and are living together as husband and wife for the last one and a half years alongwith two minor children and other family members, I am of the view that no useful purpose shall be served by prolonging the proceedings of the above mentioned case.

12. Accordingly, the entire proceedings of Case No. 1148 of 2011 (State vs. Ashok Kumar and others)
arising out of Case Crime No. 395 of 2011, under Sections 323, 498A, 506 IPC and 3/4 of D.P. Act,
P.S. Tilhar, District- Shahjahanpur, pending in the court of Civil Judge (Junior Division) Tilhar,
Shahjahanpur, are hereby quashed.
